questions.problem: If the path $C$ is a part of the curve $y=\sqrt[3]{x}$ traversed from the point $P(0,0)$ to point $Q(1,1),$ then ${\int }_{C}4y{e}^{xy}\,dx+dy=$
questions.worked_solution:
Notice that our curve is given by the explicit Cartesian equation $y=\sqrt[3]{x}.$ As a result, we obtain the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j={t}^{3}\,i+t\,j,\,t\in [0,1]\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j=3{t}^{2}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now evaluate the line integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}4y{e}^{xy}\,dx+dy & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4y{e}^{xy}\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(4y{e}^{xy}\,\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4t\cdot {e}^{{t}^{3}\cdot t}\cdot 3{t}^{2}+1\,dt \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}12{t}^{3}{e}^{{t}^{4}}+1\,dt \\  & ={[3{e}^{{t}^{4}}+t]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[3{e}^{(1)^{4}}+(1)]-[3{e}^{(0)^{4}}+(0)] \\  & =[3e+1]-[3] \\  & =3e-2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14284745/assets/a6cb0ee7062154a2489c7fa565fe6b96cd01e5f6e7a478cce39fafda0778c7a7.png)

The solid enclosed by the hemisphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2$ for $z\le 0,$ shown above, can be described in spherical polar coordinates as
questions.worked_solution:
We write the position of a point (vector) in spherical polar coordinates as $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ),$ where 

- $\rho \ge 0$ is the distance from the point to the origin,

- $\theta \in [0,2\pi )$ is the angle between the point and the positive $x$-axis, and

- $ϕ\in [0,\pi ]$ is the angle the corresponding vector makes with the positive $z$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14284745/assets/d7011de88ab3a4acb5125e5dd67e119f7cf8e1bf823c089b5f37632a5c54b971.png)

 

Notice that inside our region, the spherical polar coordinates vary within the following domains:  

- $\rho \in [0,\sqrt{2}]$

- $\theta \in [0,2\pi ]$

- $ϕ\in [\pi /2,\pi ]$

Therefore, we have

$$
\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \sqrt{2},\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,\pi /2\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

questions.problem: Use Green's theorem to evaluate ${∮}_{C}F\cdot dr,$ where $F(x,y)=⟨6{x}^{2}-xy+11,{y}^{2}+1⟩$ and $C$ is the boundary of the triangle with vertices at $(0,0),$ $(2,-1)$ and $(2,1).$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14284745/assets/007634ca34871f05cde9d44a58fcf24b1e5fd3b8c337c68f2025fb8724eef819.png)

First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∮}_{C}(6{x}^{2}-xy+11)\,dx+({y}^{2}+1)\,dy
$$

We have that $P(x,y)=6{x}^{2}-xy+11$ and $Q(x,y)={y}^{2}+1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=-x,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 2,-\frac{x}{2}\le y\le \frac{x}{2}\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(6{x}^{2}-xy+11)\,dx+({y}^{2}+1)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}[0-(-x)]\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}x\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-x/2}^{x/2}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x[y]_{-x/2}^{x/2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x(x)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\,dx \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x,y)=14x{y}^{2}$ on the region $D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le {y}^{2},\,0\le y\le 1\}$ given that the area of the region is $\frac{1}{3}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{ave}} & =\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{3})}{∬}_{D}14x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}14x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}[7{x}^{2}{y}^{2}]_{x=0}^{x={y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}7{y}^{6}\,\text{d}y \\  & =3[{y}^{7}]_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =3(1-0) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
